**

John Montagu in Innsbruck

** Discover the charm of **Tirol** through the eyes of the 4th Earl of Sandwich, **John Montagu**. In **1763**, this British aristocrat embarked on a grand tour of Europe, and his journey led him to the heart of the Alps: **Innsbruck**. Montagu’s travels were not just about sightseeing—they were a quest for adventure, culture, and, of course, fine dining. In **Innsbruck**, he would have marveled at the city’s golden-roofed **Goldenes Dachl**, a Renaissance masterpiece that still dazzles visitors today. The narrow, winding streets of the **Altstadt** (Old Town) would have whispered tales of emperors and merchants, while the scent of freshly baked **Kaiserschmarrn**—a fluffy, caramelized pancake torn into pieces—would have lured him into cozy **Gasthöfe** (traditional inns). Beyond the city, **Tirol**’s dramatic landscapes beckoned. Montagu might have ridden through the **Inntal** (Inn Valley), where lush meadows stretch toward snow-capped peaks, or taken the **Nordkettebahn**, the world’s oldest mountain railway, for a breathtaking view of the **Karwendel** and **Nordkette** ranges. The crisp mountain air and the rustic warmth of **Tiroler Gröstl**—a hearty dish of potatoes, onions, and bacon—would have been the perfect remedy after a day of exploration. For Montagu, **Innsbruck** was more than a stopover; it was a gateway to the soul of **Tirol**. Whether he sipped **Tiroler Apfelstrudel** with a glass of **Grauburgunder** or listened to the echoes of **Tiroler Volksmusik** in a lively **Beisl** (tavern), his time here would have left an indelible mark. Today, you can still follow in his footsteps—through the same streets, over the same bridges, and into the same stories that have captivated travelers for centuries. **

Plan your own journey to Innsbruck and experience Tirol like John Montagu did—where history, nature, and tradition collide.

**
